why:
phase-467 Row 8. The Rust half of `rclc_node_get_graph_guard_condition` -- a guard condition the BACKEND triggers when the ROS graph changes, which is upstream's `rcl_node_get_graph_guard_condition` under this project's guard-condition shape.

OURS-ONLY against rclrs, which has no graph-change surface at all: rclrs exposes no `Node::get_graph_change_event`, no graph guard condition and no wait set, so there is nothing for this to be a rename OF. It is not an `extension` in the "ROS 2 has none" sense either, because rcl does have the capability -- what rcl has is a RETURNED borrowed handle you add to a wait set, and two platform constraints rule that out here: no allocator at the entity seam (RFC-0018/0019 -- every entity is caller storage with the status in the return) and no wait set (RFC-0002 -- one executor per RTOS task, `cpp:WaitSet` declined). So the guard is CREATED, exactly as `register_guard_condition_on` creates one, and differs only in who pulls the trigger: the application there, the backend's discovery path here.

The C twin `c:node_get_graph_guard_condition` (node/) carries the full envelope, the backend measurements and the live acceptance. Read it there rather than in a second copy here.

The NODE-BOUND form, and the one the C entry point calls. The registered slot takes that node's default `SchedContext`, which is what "the node owns it" has to mean for a callback sharing one executor with every other tier in the image (RFC-0047) -- the same reason `register_guard_condition_on` exists.
